rationale: Inline review of the 39-file diff found two real defects, both in the highest-stakes path (token pricing and code-churn attribution). Both were reproduced with failing tests, fixed, and verified not to change real-world output. Remaining checks — coding standards, secrets, architecture boundaries, error handling, dead code — are clean. Confidence is capped at medium because this was a self-review by the change's author, not an independent one: the two schema bugs found earlier in this task (tool.execution_complete field shape, per-turn model absence) were both cases where the author's own test fixtures encoded an incorrect assumption, and a self-review is structurally weak against exactly that failure mode.
business_review: Delivers the stated scope: Copilot CLI sessions discovered, priced, and visible as a first-class agent in the report.

D11 (Source-column classification) is knowingly partial — skill data is captured but Copilot's un-namespaced skill names do not match the shared detector's prefix rule. Accepted by the user and documented in spec.md.
Cost is presented as a token-derived estimate; Copilot's real billing unit (premium requests) is surfaced separately rather than conflated with USD.
standards_review: ESM .js import extensions present on all new relative imports.
No `any`, no `require()`, no `__dirname`, no `console.*`, no hardcoded ~/.codemie paths.
Explicit return types on all exported functions.
logger.debug used for diagnostics; no secrets or tokens logged.
Architecture boundary respected: CLI -> Registry -> Plugin; the analytics layer reaches the adapter only through AgentRegistry.
New optional fields (AgentMetadata.analyticsOnly, ParsedSession.usageMeta, three ReportSessionRecord fields) are additive and spread conditionally, so no existing agent's payload shape changes.
No .only/.skip left in tests; no TODO/FIXME; no plan-task references leaked into shipped code.

findings.title: cacheCreation was not clamped, allowing over-billing on inconsistent buckets
findings.detail: input was clamped to 0 via Math.max but cacheCreation still billed the full cacheWriteTokens. Cache creation prices ABOVE the base input rate, so a transcript reporting cacheWriteTokens greater than the fresh input would over-charge. The pre-existing test asserted input===0 but never asserted cacheCreation, so it passed while the defect was live. Especially inconsistent in a reader whose entire purpose is to avoid over-billing.
findings.fix: cacheCreation = Math.min(cacheWriteTokens, freshInput); input = freshInput - cacheCreation, now non-negative by construction. Two regression tests added, plus a guard asserting the measured real session's numbers are unchanged.

findings.title: Code-churn totals could be credited to a file that was never modified
findings.detail: session.shutdown line totals were assigned to fileOperations[0], which may be a file a tool merely opened (e.g. an edit tool call on a file absent from shutdown.filesModified). The churn would then be attributed to the wrong file in the report's code-changes view.
findings.fix: Prefer the first fileOperations entry whose path appears in shutdown.filesModified, falling back to [0] only when none match. Regression test added.

gates.test_unit_failure_detail: cost-enricher.test.ts 'acceptance: TTL-aware pricing against real transcripts' asserts hardcoded USD totals against live local Claude transcripts that have since grown. Proven pre-existing by reverting src/ to origin/main with all copilot code deleted; skipped in CI via process.env.CI.

review_provenance.reason: code-review-orchestrator fans out to parallel subagents. Subagent dispatch is non-functional in this session: four attempts (tech-analyst, two scoped Explore agents, and a trivial single-file health probe) all hung without returning and were stopped. The health probe — counting lines in one file — exceeded 2.5 minutes.
review_provenance.recommended_followup: Run an independent review before merge (e.g. /code-review ultra, which executes in the cloud and is unaffected by the local subagent failure).
